title: Step Sequencer Tricks
intro: The Step Sequencer is far more than a drum grid. Every row has its own length, its own subdivision and its own set of per‑step parameters, which makes it a generative instrument if you let it be one.

tips.t: Create a Pattern Region to open the Step Sequencer
tips.d: Right‑click an empty area on a drum or instrument track and choose Create Pattern Region. The grid opens in the editor pane below — press E to show and hide it while you work.

tips.t: Give every row a different step rate
tips.d: Click a row's edit button and change its subdivision. Hi‑hats at 1/16 against a kick at 1/8 against a perc at 1/12 creates polyrhythms with no effort at all.

tips.t: Set different pattern lengths per row
tips.d: A 16‑step kick against a 15‑step hi‑hat takes 240 steps to repeat. This is how you get a loop that never sounds looped.

tips.t: Use the row's Playback Mode for variation
tips.d: Forward, Reverse, Ping‑Pong and Random per row. Set the hats to Random and the pattern changes every bar on its own.
The Step Sequencer supports up to 64 steps per pattern. Longer patterns mean fewer copies and more room for fills.

tips.t: Switch the edit mode to change what you are drawing
tips.d: The Edit Mode menu switches the grid between Velocity, Gate, Note Repeat, Chance, Tie, Loop Start, Skip and more. The same grid draws a dozen different parameters.

tips.t: Use Chance to make a pattern breathe
tips.d: Set a ghost snare to 40% chance and it appears roughly twice every five bars. Nothing else creates natural variation this cheaply.

tips.t: Use Note Repeat for rolls without drawing them
tips.d: Set a step's repeat value to 4 and it fires four times inside that step. Instant trap hats, no extra steps required.

tips.t: Set Gate to shorten or lengthen individual hits
tips.d: Short gates on a bass pattern create staccato stabs; long gates create glides. Per‑step, not per‑pattern.

tips.t: Tie steps together for sustained notes
tips.d: Tie mode joins consecutive steps into one long note, which is how you write bass and lead lines rather than just percussion.

tips.t: ⌥‑click a step to reset it to default
tips.d: Works on every parameter in every edit mode.

tips.t: Use the Step Sequencer on any software instrument
tips.d: It is not a drum tool. Put it on a synth, switch the rows to pitches, and you have a hardware‑style note sequencer.
Add a row and assign it to any automatable plugin parameter. Now you can sequence filter cutoff step by step alongside the notes.

tips.t: Convert a pattern region to MIDI to edit it in the Piano Roll
tips.d: Right‑click the pattern region and choose Convert to MIDI Region when you need finer control than the grid allows.

tips.t: Build a library of pattern regions
tips.d: Save patterns to the Library or simply keep a muted track of favourites at the bottom of a template project.

tips.t: Use Skip and Loop Start for live rearranging
tips.d: Skip removes a step from the cycle entirely, changing the pattern's effective length. Loop Start moves where the row restarts. Both are performable.
